doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: 52nd Street, jam sessions and getting fired from jobs
summary: Staying late on 52nd Street, sitting in with Dizzy's big band, hearing Bird, Hawkins and Tatum.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Those two years you were in New York from late ’46 to ’48 when you left with McShann, did you go to jam sessions?

Oh yeah, I went to jam sessions, sure. I used to hang out on 52nd Street. I was working at Radio City Music Hall, and I was supposed to be there at a certain time, but many nights I was late because I was on 52nd Street. So, one night they fired me, so I walked right across the street to the RCA building and got a job there. This is the lowest rung of the ladder, cleaning up the theaters after the place closers. A migrant worker, you could call it. I would hang out there on 52nd Street all the time. I would sit in with Dizzy’s band. Dizzy had a big band at a place called the Spotlight. I would sit in there, and next door was the Downbeat, and Bird, with Miles, was there. I would go and listen to them. It’s hard to get to work on time [laughs]. Right down the street was my gig, but damn!
So, going to New York was probably more spectacular than the first time you went to Los Angeles?

Yeah, listening to the giants across the street was Coleman Hawkins, and down the street was Art Tatum, Erroll Garner, all these people. What can be better than that? The only thing that could be better was my own head because I didn’t know what to listen for really. When you’re that age, everything sounds good, but you have to learn. That’s part of it.
